question.text: In a FLOATING-RATE bond, the bond's coupon resets periodically. The MAXIMUM duration (interest-rate sensitivity) at any point is approximately:

answer.text: The remaining time until the next coupon reset

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that a floater's coupon resets periodically with the underlying index, and that its maximum duration at any given point is only the remaining time until the underlying index is reset. The Trap: Using full bond maturity confuses a floater with a fixed-rate bond. Once the coupon resets to the current market index, sensitivity is reset, so duration cannot accumulate over the full life of the bond. Note: Page 344 sets out the floater reset rule and the maximum-duration limit between reset dates.
